info.description:
# Mailsoftly API Documentation

Mailsoftly is an email marketing and automation platform. This API allows you to manage contacts,
contact lists, tags, custom fields, email campaigns, and unsubscribe preferences programmatically.

## Authentication

Two credentials are accepted, both in the `Authorization` header.

**1. API key (company access key).** Send the raw token, with no `Bearer` prefix:

```
Authorization: YOUR_API_KEY
```

Generate one from your Mailsoftly dashboard under **Settings → API Keys**. Keys created from
now on are stored hashed (shown once, at creation) and expire one year after they are issued.
Older keys keep working and do not expire. A key can be limited to the IP addresses or ranges
your servers call from; a call from anywhere else gets `401` with `ip_not_allowed`.

**2. OAuth 2.1 access token.** Apps that authorize through Mailsoftly send the token with the
`Bearer` prefix:

```
Authorization: Bearer your-oauth-access-token
```

Discovery documents live at `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` and
`/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`. Only the authorization code flow with PKCE is supported.

## Scopes

Every operation declares the scope it needs as `x-scope`:

| Scope | Grants |
|-------|--------|
| `contacts:read` | Read contacts, lists, tags, custom fields, segments |
| `contacts:write` | Create and update the same, including list membership |
| `campaigns:read` | Read campaigns, drafts and their status |
| `campaigns:draft` | Create and edit drafts, templates, assets and settings that do not deliver mail |
| `campaigns:send` | Send or schedule campaigns, send tests, activate automations |
| `sms:send` | Send text messages (SMS), read their status, manage the SMS status webhook. API keys only |
| `suppressions:write` | Change global email unsubscribe state |
| `account:read` | Read account profile, senders, signatures, integrations, team |
| `account:write` | Invite teammates, change their roles, revoke invitations |

An OAuth token that is missing the scope an operation declares gets `403` with a
`WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="insufficient_scope"` header. API keys are full access by
default, so they satisfy every scope unless they were issued with a narrower set.
`sms:send` is held by API keys only, never by an OAuth app: a key limited to it can call
`send_transactional_sms` and `get_message_status` for text messages, and the `*_status_webhook` calls with `channel: "sms"`, and nothing else.

## Base URL

```
https://app.mailsoftly.com/api/v3
```

## Rate limits

Limits are per credential (API key or OAuth token), not per IP address, so an integration never shares a budget with another customer behind the same network.

| Bucket | Limit | Applies to |
|--------|-------|------------|
| Requests | 600 per 5 minutes | Every endpoint |
| Sends | 600 per hour | `send_email`, `schedule_email`, `send_transactional_email`, `send_transactional_sms`, `start_ab_test` |

Every response carries `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining` and `RateLimit-Reset` (seconds until the window resets). Send endpoints add `RateLimit-Send-Limit`, `RateLimit-Send-Remaining` and `RateLimit-Send-Reset`. Over the limit you get `429 Too Many Requests` with a `Retry-After` header and the standard error body; wait that long and retry. A per-address backstop of 3,000 requests per 5 minutes applies across all credentials, which is what bounds a caller with no valid key.

## Request size

- A request body may be up to **10 MB**. Larger bodies get `413` before they are parsed.
- Array parameters have per-call ceilings: `contacts` in `add_contacts_to_contact_list` up to 1,000; `tags` in `assign_tags_to_contact` up to 100; `mailLists` in `create_emails` up to 50 drafts, each with up to 30,150 `recipients` and 20 `attaches`. Over a ceiling you get `413` with `max_items` in the body. Split the call, or import large audiences with `import_contacts` and pass `contact_list_id`.

## Pagination

List endpoints take `page` (from 1) and `per_page`. Contact listings (`get_contacts`, `get_contact_list_contacts`, `search_contacts`) accept `per_page` up to **500**; other lists up to 100. When you pass either parameter the response is an envelope: `{..., page, per_page, total, has_more}`. Keep requesting the next page while `has_more` is true.

Contact listings called without `page` or `per_page` keep their original shape for existing integrations, capped at 10,000 rows. The response then carries `X-Total-Count`, and when the account holds more than the cap, `X-Truncated: true` and a `Link: <...>; rel="next"` header pointing at page 2. New integrations should always paginate.

## Error Responses

Every error answers with JSON in the same envelope:

```json
{
  "status": "error",
  "code": "domain_not_authenticated",
  "error": "The sending domain example.com has not finished authentication, so email from news@example.com cannot go out yet. Add the DNS records shown on the Domains page in Mailsoftly; sending works as soon as they verify.",
  "unlock_paths": [
    { "id": "sending_domain", "label": "Authenticate your sending domain (add its DNS records).", "url": "https://app.mailsoftly.com/en/company_profile/123/domains" }
  ]
}
```

- `code` is stable and machine-readable. Branch on it, not on the sentence. Endpoints with a specific reason name it (`contact_not_found`, `recipient_suppressed`, `sending_limit_reached`); every other error carries the code for its HTTP status (`invalid_request`, `not_found`, `unauthorized` and so on).
- `error` is one sentence for a person: what went wrong and what to do next. Show it to your user as is. Older endpoints can return a list of validation sentences here instead of one.
- `unlock_paths` (when present) lists the ways to fix an account-level block, in the order to try them. Each has an `id`, a `label` and a `url` into the Mailsoftly app.
- `gate` (when present) explains a sending block in more detail: `blocked`, `level` (`account` or `campaign`), `reason`, `message` and `unlock_paths`.
- `required_scope` (on 403) names the permission the key or token is missing.
- `allowed_methods` (on 405) lists the methods the path accepts.

| Status | Meaning | What to do |
|--------|---------|------------|
| 400 | The request body or a parameter could not be read | Fix the JSON or the parameter named in `error` |
| 401 | No API key, an invalid or expired key, or the account cannot use the API (`invalid_api_key`, `api_key_expired`, `invalid_token`, `api_access_off`, `scoped_key_required`, `ip_not_allowed`) | Send a valid key in the `Authorization` header; create one under Settings > API. For `ip_not_allowed`, call from an address the key allows or create a key that allows it. For `api_access_off`, contact us |
| 403 | The key is valid but lacks the permission this endpoint needs (`insufficient_scope`, see `required_scope`) | Use a key that includes that scope |
| 404 | The record or the endpoint does not exist (`*_not_found`, `endpoint_not_found`) | Check the id; list endpoints show valid ids |
| 405 | The endpoint exists but takes another HTTP method (`method_not_allowed`) | Use the method in `allowed_methods`, also sent in the `Allow` header |
| 409 | The request conflicts with the record's current state | Read the record again and retry |
| 413 | Request body over 10 MB, or an array parameter over its per-call ceiling (`max_items` in the body) | Split the request |
| 422 | The request is understood but cannot be done as it stands: a missing or invalid field, or an account or sending rule | Fix what `error` names, or follow `unlock_paths` |
| 429 | Rate limit exceeded (`rate_limited`) | Wait for `Retry-After` seconds, then retry |
| 500 | Something failed on our side (`internal_error`) | Retry later; contact us if it continues |

Only 429 and 5xx are worth retrying unchanged. A 4xx needs a change to the request or the account first.

## Webhook signatures

Mailsoftly sends two kinds of webhook: a **Send webhook** step in an automation (contact data, see *Automation webhooks* below) and the **status webhook** of the transactional API (`send_transactional_email`, `send_transactional_sms`, `set_status_webhook`). Both are signed the same way, so one verification function covers all of them. The signature lets your server confirm a request came from Mailsoftly, was not changed on the way, and is not a replay.

### Signature headers

| Header | Value |
|--------|-------|
| `X-Mailsoftly-Signature` | `t=<unix time>,v1=<hex>`, where `t` is when this attempt was sent, in Unix seconds, and `v1` is the HMAC-SHA256 of `<t>.<raw request body>` keyed with your webhook secret, hex-encoded. |
| `X-Mailsoftly-Event-Id` | Unique event id, such as `evt_3f9a1c7e5b2d8a4f6c0e1b9d`. A retried delivery keeps the same id, so de-duplicate on it. |
| `X-Mailsoftly-Event` | What the request is: `automation.webhook` for a Send webhook delivery, `webhook.verification` for the endpoint check, or the event name (`sent`, `delivered`, `bounced`, `complained`, `failed`, `replied`, `test`) for a transactional status event. |

### Your secret

Every secret starts with `whsec_`, and the whole string, prefix included, is the HMAC key: use it exactly as shown, without decoding it. Libraries built for other webhook schemes that base64-decode the secret will not match. A Send webhook step has its own secret, shown in the step's settings in the automation editor (show, copy, rotate). A status webhook's secret is returned by `set_status_webhook` when the webhook is created and when you rotate it; the email and SMS status webhooks each have their own. Rotating a secret takes effect at once, with no overlap: requests are signed with the new secret from that moment, so give it to your server right away.

### Verifying a signature

1. Read the raw request body exactly as received, before any JSON parsing.
2. Split `X-Mailsoftly-Signature` on `,` into `key=value` pairs: `t` is the timestamp, `v1` the signature.
3. Reject the request if `t` is more than 5 minutes away from your clock.
4. Compute the HMAC-SHA256 of `<t>.<raw body>` (the timestamp, a dot, then the body) with your webhook secret and hex-encode it.
5. Compare it with `v1` using a constant-time comparison. Accept the request if any `v1` value matches.

```ruby
require "openssl"

def mailsoftly_signature_valid?(signature_header, raw_body, secret)
  pairs = signature_header.to_s.split(",").map { |pair| pair.strip.split("=", 2) }
  timestamp = pairs.find { |key, _| key == "t" }&.last
  signatures = pairs.select { |key, _| key == "v1" }.map(&:last)
  return false if timestamp.nil? || signatures.empty?
  return false if (Time.now.to_i - timestamp.to_i).abs > 300

  expected = OpenSSL::HMAC.hexdigest("SHA256", secret, "#{timestamp}.#{raw_body}")
  signatures.any? { |signature| OpenSSL.secure_compare(signature.to_s, expected) }
end

# mailsoftly_signature_valid?(request.headers["X-Mailsoftly-Signature"], request.raw_post, ENV["MAILSOFTLY_WEBHOOK_SECRET"])
```

```javascript
const crypto = require("crypto");

function mailsoftlySignatureValid(signatureHeader, rawBody, secret) {
  const pairs = (signatureHeader || "").split(",").map((pair) => pair.trim().split("="));
  const timestamp = (pairs.find(([key]) => key === "t") || [])[1];
  const signatures = pairs.filter(([key]) => key === "v1").map(([, value]) => value || "");
  if (!timestamp || signatures.length === 0) return false;
  if (Math.abs(Date.now() / 1000 - Number(timestamp)) > 300) return false;

  const expected = crypto.createHmac("sha256", secret).update(`${timestamp}.${rawBody}`).digest("hex");
  return signatures.some((signature) => signature.length === expected.length &&
    crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(signature), Buffer.from(expected)));
}

// mailsoftlySignatureValid(req.get("X-Mailsoftly-Signature"), rawBody, process.env.MAILSOFTLY_WEBHOOK_SECRET)
```

v1:   d9ce1d372b823dad14856fb76285af7cdc8ee059fdfc8949648cf1b644db8edb
```

v1:   7f233d7ce4e00fd502155bae0e95a779472a0c7627c1f26ebbb046e781612da4
```

## Automation webhooks

A **Send webhook** step in an automation POSTs contact data as JSON to an https address you choose. Every request is signed as described under *Webhook signatures*: the HMAC key is the step's own secret from the step's settings, `X-Mailsoftly-Event` is `automation.webhook` for a delivery and `webhook.verification` for the endpoint check below, and `X-Mailsoftly-Event-Id` stays the same when a delivery is retried.

### Verifying your endpoint

Mailsoftly asks your endpoint to prove the address is yours. When you save a new or changed URL, and whenever you choose **Verify URL** in the step's settings, Mailsoftly sends one signed request with the step's own custom headers:

```json
{"type": "webhook.verification", "challenge": "3q2-7wEXAMPLEvalue"}
```

Answer within 10 seconds with a 2xx status and the challenge in the body, either as the bare value (`text/plain`) or as JSON:

```json
{"challenge": "3q2-7wEXAMPLEvalue"}
```

Redirects are not followed. Until the endpoint answers, the step shows **Not verified yet** and still sends contact data. When verification is enforced, an unverified step sends nothing until its endpoint answers. Changing the URL clears the verification and sends a new check. Treat a body with `"type": "webhook.verification"` as a check, not as contact data.

Catch hook addresses that an automation platform creates for you count as verified as soon as you save them, and no check is sent to them: Zapier (`hooks.zapier.com`), Make (`hook.<region>.make.com`, `hook.integromat.com`), n8n Cloud (`<name>.app.n8n.cloud/webhook/...`, `hooks.n8n.cloud`), Pipedream (`<id>.m.pipedream.net`), IFTTT (`maker.ifttt.com`), Slack incoming webhooks (`hooks.slack.com/services/...`) and your own Mailsoftly catch URLs (`/catch/...`). Such an address is issued by the platform to your account there, so it already shows the address is yours. The step shows **Created by** the platform's name, and its requests are signed like any other.

Use this endpoint to verify that your token is valid before making other API calls.

Creates an automation as a **draft** with the same vocabulary as the in-app builder: one trigger, optional extra start events, an optional entry filter, and an ordered list of steps that can branch. Nothing runs until the automation is activated with `POST /update_automation_status`.

## Trigger

`trigger.event` picks the start event. Some events need a target field.

| event | needs | starts when |
|---|---|---|
| `contact_created` | | a contact is created |
| `contact_updated` | | a contact is updated |
| `tag_added` | `tag_id` | that tag is applied to a contact |
| `list_added` | `contact_list_id` | a contact joins that list |
| `form_submitted` | `soft_form_id` | that form is submitted |
| `contact_unsubscribed` | | a contact unsubscribes |
| `webhook` | `endpoint_id` | JSON is posted to that endpoint (first step must be `create_or_find_contact`) |
| `campaign_sent` | `campaign_id` | that campaign is sent |
| `specific_date` | `when: "now"` or `scheduled_at` | on activation, or at the given time |
| `contact_date_field` | `date_field_key`, optional `days_before` or `days_after` (0 to 365), `yearly` | that many days before or after a date field on the contact |
| `birthday` | optional `days_before` (team reminder lead time) | the contact's birthday comes up |
| `inactive_contacts` / `active_contacts` | `days` | a contact has been inactive / active for that long |

`extra_triggers` adds parallel start events: `[{ "event": "form_submitted", "soft_form_id": 12 }]` (events: contact_created, contact_updated, tag_added, list_added, form_submitted, contact_unsubscribed).

`entry_filter` limits who may enter: `{ "groups": [{ "join": "and", "conditions": [{ "field": "country", "operator": "equals", "value": "US" }] }] }`. Fields are the contact fields and your custom fields; operators: equals, does_not_equal, contains, starts_with, ends_with, does_not_contain, is_empty, is_not_empty.

## Steps

Each step has a `kind` plus the fields for that kind. Steps run in order.

| kind | fields |
|---|---|
| `send_email` | `email_template_id`, optional `subject`, `sender_id` or `email_sender_id`, `send_at_best_time` |
| `add_tags` / `remove_tags` | `tag_ids` |
| `add_to_lists` / `remove_from_lists` | `contact_list_ids` |
| `remove_from_all_lists` | |
| `wait` | `duration`, `unit` (days or minutes) |
| `wait_until` | `case` (submitted_form + `soft_form_id`, opened_email, clicked_link, check_contact_field + `conditions`), `max_wait`, `unit` |
| `send_webhook` | `url` (https) |
| `notify` | `emails` or `user_ids`, optional `subject`, `body` |
| `update_contact` | `fields` (field to value); webhook-triggered automations only |
| `create_or_find_contact` | `email_key` (key of the email in the webhook payload) |
| `condition` | `case` and branches `yes` / `no` (see below) |
| `ab_split` | `percent`, `metric` (opens or clicks), `decide_after_days` (1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 14) and branches `a` / `b` |
| `multi_split` | `field`, `lanes` (values) and `branches` keyed by lane plus `else` |
| `stop` | |

## Branching

A `condition` step carries a `case`: opened_email, clicked_link, check_contact_field (with `conditions`, same shape as the entry filter), is_unsubscribed, engaged_recently (with `days`), entered_via (with `event`), submitted_form (with `soft_form_id`), created_by. Its `yes` and `no` arrays hold ordinary steps and may nest further conditions, up to four levels deep. `ab_split` works the same with `a` and `b`; `multi_split` with one array per lane and an `else` lane.

## Limits

Free accounts that have not verified a sending channel may keep a small number of automations; the response then carries a `gate` with `level: "plan"` and the upgrade or verify path. Activation needs a verified account and every step complete; the response lists `missing_trigger_fields` and per-step `complete` flags naming what is incomplete.

post.description:
Creates one or more email drafts: a single draft, or several at once through the `mailLists` array.

**Audience**: give it one of three ways:
- `contact_list_id`: one existing list, OR
- `contact_list_ids` and/or `segment_ids`: several lists and segments. Everyone on any of them gets the campaign once (an address on two lists, in any letter case, gets one email and counts once against the sending limit). `exclude_contact_list_ids` and `exclude_segment_ids` leave people out, and an exclusion always wins over an inclusion. Include and exclude entries together are capped at 15. Recipients are worked out when the campaign is sent, so people added to a list after the draft is made are included. Sending to more than one list or segment, or excluding any, has to be turned on for the account (`audience_not_enabled` otherwise). OR
- `recipients`: an array of **recipient objects** (`{ email, first_name?, last_name? }`). A new contact list named `"List (created via API at YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS)"` is created automatically and its ID is returned in the response as `contact_list_id`.

`contact_list_id` and `contact_list_ids` together, or `recipients` together with any of the list and segment fields, is refused with `audience_conflict`. An unknown list id is refused with `contact_list_not_found`, an unknown segment id with `segment_not_found`, more than 15 entries with `audience_too_many`. Each draft in the response carries `audience` (the included and excluded lists and segments by id and name, and `estimated_recipients`) and `contact_list_id`, which is the one list for a single-list audience, the first included list otherwise, and null when only segments are included.

**⚠️ Important: asynchronous list population.** With `recipients`, the response returns immediately with an **empty** auto-created list. A background job then (a) upserts each recipient as a contact and (b) adds those contacts to the new list, and finally flips the draft to `ready_to_send: true`. This typically takes **5-15 seconds**, up to **~60 seconds** under load. `POST /send_email` returns `422 EmailDraft is not ready for sending yet` until `GET /email_status?id={draft_id}` reports `ready_to_send: true`.

**Recipient format matters.** Each item must be an **object** with at least `email`. Plain-string arrays (e.g. `["a@b.com"]`) are silently skipped by the background job, which will leave the auto-created list empty and result in a send to zero recipients.

**Attachments**: an array of objects with `url` and `filename`. URLs must be publicly accessible HTTP/HTTPS links and are also fetched asynchronously; the same `ready_to_send` gate applies.

**Choosing the from address.** `GET /list_senders` returns every address the account can send from, and each entry names the parameter that selects it in `usable_as`:
- `sender_id`: a teammate on an authenticated domain (`kind: "user"`).
- `email_sender_id`: a connected Gmail/Microsoft mailbox or the shared sending address (`kind: "gmail_mailbox"`, `"outlook_mailbox"`, `"shared_fallback"`).

**Exactly one** of the two is accepted; both together is rejected. With neither, the account's default sender (`default_sender_id` in the `list_senders` response) is used. When `email_sender_id` names a connected mailbox, `reply_to` is locked to that mailbox's own address and any value in the request is ignored, exactly as the composer locks the field.

**Workflow summary:** `POST /create_emails`, then `GET /email_status` until `ready_to_send: true`, then `POST /send_email`.

get.description:
Returns the current status of an email draft and whether it's ready to send.

**Status values:**
- `Draft`: draft is being prepared
- `Sent`: email has been sent
- `sending`: email is currently being sent (in queue)
- `ready_to_send: true` means the draft can be sent via `POST /send_email`

**Polling guidance.** When a draft is created via `POST /create_emails` with `recipients` or `attaches`, a background job upserts the contacts, attaches the files, and only then flips `ready_to_send` to `true`. That takes **5-15 seconds** in the typical case and up to **~60 seconds** under load, so a client polling every ~2 seconds for up to 90 seconds covers it. Drafts created against an existing `contact_list_id` with no attachments are `ready_to_send: true` immediately.

**Sender lane.** The response also carries a `sender` object: `lane` (`gmail`, `outlook`, `domain` or `shared`), the `from` address, and `authorized`, which is false when the campaign sends from a mailbox another teammate connected or from a domain that has not finished DNS authentication. `ready_to_send` is unchanged and means the draft itself is assembled.

level.description: Which layer the state belongs to: 'account' the whole account, 'campaign' this campaign, 'plan' a plan entitlement.

reason.description: Machine readable reason code. The sender lane adds three: 'sender_not_authorized' when the campaign sends from a mailbox another teammate connected with their own Google or Microsoft account, 'oauth_mailbox_unsupported' when the action has no equivalent on such a mailbox, and 'domain_authentication_required' when the from domain has not finished DNS authentication.

post.description:
Used by the Mailsoftly app for Canva. Downloads the email design a Canva user exported (the short-lived ZIP link Canva gives the app) and creates a campaign draft from it, the same way Import your design does in Mailsoftly: the images go to the connected user's image library, the HTML is kept as designed, and the unsubscribe, update preferences and view in browser placeholders of the export become Mailsoftly merge tags. The draft has no subject, sender or audience yet; the user finishes it on the campaign page that `url` opens.

**Credentials.** An OAuth access token with `campaigns:draft`, issued to a user who can edit campaigns. The draft and its images belong to that user. API keys are refused with `403 oauth_required`. Every call also carries the Canva user token in the `X-Canva-User-Token` header.

**Limits.** Up to 30 calls per 10 minutes per connection, on top of the general request limit (`429 rate_limited`, with `Retry-After`). The export can be up to 15 MB.

**Publishing again.** With a valid `design_token`, publishing the same Canva design again updates the draft it created last time (`200`, `updated: true`): the email HTML is replaced and the name is kept unless `name` is sent. That happens only while the draft is still an unsent, unscheduled HTML draft whose email has not been edited in Mailsoftly since the last publish; otherwise a new draft is created (`201`) and later publishes update that one. Without a `design_token`, or with one that does not verify, every call creates a new draft.

**Errors.** Every error carries a stable `code`:

| code | Status | Meaning |
|------|--------|---------|
| `oauth_required` | 403 | Called with an API key instead of an OAuth access token |
| `campaign_edit_not_allowed` | 403 | The connected user cannot create campaigns |
| `canva_token_missing` | 401 | No `X-Canva-User-Token` header |
| `canva_token_invalid` | 401 | The Canva user token is not signed for the Mailsoftly app for Canva |
| `canva_token_expired` | 401 | The Canva user token has expired: get a new one and retry |
| `canva_keys_unavailable` | 503 | The Canva user token could not be checked right now: retry in a minute |
| `canva_not_configured` | 503 | Publishing from Canva is not available |
| `bundle_url_required` | 422 | `bundle_url` is missing |
| `bundle_url_invalid` | 422 | `bundle_url` is not an https link on export-download.canva.com |
| `bundle_unavailable` | 502 | The export could not be downloaded, usually because the link expired: export again |
| `empty`, `file_too_large`, `html_too_large`, `not_html`, `unsupported_file`, `zip_unreadable`, `zip_encrypted`, `zip_no_html`, `zip_many_html`, `zip_too_many_files`, `zip_too_large_unpacked` | 422 | The export could not be read as an email |
| `save_failed` | 422 | The draft could not be saved |

post.description:
Sends an existing email draft. The draft must be in a ready state, which `GET /email_status` reports.

**Important:** This endpoint only works with draft IDs created via `POST /create_emails`. For one email to one person, with a message id and delivery status events, use `POST /send_transactional_email` instead.

The send is asynchronous. The email is queued for delivery and processed in the background.

**When `422 EmailDraft is not ready for sending yet` comes back,** the background job that populates recipients/attachments has not finished. Common causes:
- The send followed `POST /create_emails` too quickly; `GET /email_status` reports `ready_to_send: true` once the job finishes (typically 5-15s).
- `recipients` arrived as **plain strings** instead of objects (`{ email: "..." }`). Plain-string items are silently skipped by the background job, so the list stays empty and the draft does not become ready; a draft with object-form recipients does.
- The draft is in an excluded status (`in_queue`, `review`, `email_test_in_review`).

**The from address decides the lane.** A campaign whose sender is a Gmail or Microsoft mailbox a teammate connected goes out through that mailbox, so only that teammate's OAuth token can send it; a company access key names nobody and gets `403` with `gate.reason: "sender_not_authorized"`. A campaign on one of the account's own sending domains needs that domain authenticated first, otherwise `403` with `gate.reason: "domain_authentication_required"`. Every response carries a `sender` object with the `lane`, the `from` address and `authorized`. `POST /update_email` moves a campaign onto another address with `sender_id` or `email_sender_id` from `GET /list_senders`.

post.description:
Sends one email to one recipient and answers at once with a `message_id`. Use it for application email: notifications, confirmations, reminders, one-time links.

Content comes from a saved template (`template_id`; merge tags render with the recipient's contact fields) or from `subject` with `body`. The recipient becomes, or updates, a contact of the account; `first_name`, `last_name` and `fields` (values for custom fields that already exist, see `create_custom_field`) are written to that contact before the email renders.

The send goes through the same checks as every email from the account: suppressions and unsubscribes (`422 recipient_suppressed`), sending limits and account review. `202` with `state: "queued"` means it is on its way; `state: "held"` means it waits for review and leaves once released. Outside test mode, transactional email leaves from an authenticated domain sender; a connected Gmail or Microsoft mailbox is refused with `422 mailbox_sender_not_supported`.

Pass `idempotency_key` to make retries safe: a second call with the same key returns the first message (`200`, `idempotent_replay: true`) instead of sending again.

**Test mode.** While your own sending domain is still being authenticated, our team can put the account in API test mode so you can build and test your integration; there is nothing to turn on in the app. In test mode every email from this operation leaves from the Mailsoftly test address (returned as `from`; your organization's name is shown as the sender name, and replies go to `reply_to`, or to the sender you chose when none is passed), to any recipient, up to 100 emails a day. Past that, the call is refused with `422 test_mode_limit_reached` and `resets_at` says when the allowance returns. `message_id`, `get_message_status` and the status webhook work as in production, and every response and event carries `test_mode: true`. Test mode ends on its own as soon as your first domain is authenticated, or after 30 days; from then on email leaves from your own domain under the production rules.

**Archive copy.** If your records policy needs every email exactly as sent, our team can set a records mailbox on the account; there is nothing to turn on in the app or the API. Each transactional email, including those sent in test mode, is then also delivered to that mailbox as the same message: same `message_id`, headers and body. Campaigns and automations are not copied. The copy has no status of its own, does not count against your sending limits, and a problem with the records mailbox never changes the recipient's status. One-time links and codes are copied like any other content. Every send response carries `archive_copy`, true while a mailbox is set.

**Message type and the unsubscribe link.** Pass `message_type` to say what kind of email this is: `transactional` (the default) for a service message or a notice the recipient must receive, `marketing` for anything promotional. On a Regulated Environment account a transactional email leaves without the unsubscribe link in the footer and without the List-Unsubscribe headers; the footer still shows your organization, its address and the footer sentence set on your account. A marketing email keeps the link and headers, and so do campaigns and automations, on every account. On other accounts both types keep the link. The type is stored on the message and returned by get_message_status, so your records show which emails went out without a link. An address that unsubscribed earlier is still refused with `recipient_suppressed`, whatever the type.

**Tracking.** On a Regulated Environment account a transactional email leaves untracked: no open pixel, no rewritten links and no tracking parameters added to your links, whatever the account's tracking setting. A marketing email follows the account's setting, and so do campaigns and automations; on other accounts both types follow it. Tracked links use the account's branded tracking domain when it has one. Opens and clicks are never sent to the status webhook; they appear only in Mailsoftly's own reports.

**Refusals.** When an email cannot go out, nothing is sent or stored, and the answer is `422` with one of these codes. Each `error` sentence says what to fix, and `unlock_paths` links to where.

| code | Meaning | Fix |
|------|---------|-----|
| `invalid_to` | `to` is not one valid address | Pass a single email address |
| `content_required` | No template and no body, or the template has no content | Pass `template_id`, or `subject` and `body` |
| `subject_required` | No subject and the template has none | Pass `subject` |
| `invalid_body_format` | `body_format` is not `content` or `html` | Use one of the two |
| `invalid_message_type` | `message_type` is not `transactional` or `marketing` | Use one of the two |
| `embedded_image_not_supported` | The body has an embedded (base64) image | Upload the image (`POST /upload_file`) and link it by URL |
| `recipient_suppressed` | The address unsubscribed, bounced, complained or is suppressed | Do not send to it; the recipient can resubscribe through a preference link |
| `domain_not_authenticated` | The sender's domain has not finished authentication | Add the domain's DNS records in Mailsoftly, or send from another sender (`GET /list_senders`) |
| `domain_authentication_broken` | The domain was authenticated but a DNS record changed | Fix the record shown on the Domains page |
| `own_domain_required` | The account has no authenticated domain, and the shared address is for testing only | Authenticate your own domain |
| `test_mode_limit_reached` | The account is in API test mode and today's allowance of 100 test emails is used | Wait for `resets_at`, or authenticate your own domain to leave test mode |
| `mailbox_sender_not_supported` | The sender is a connected Gmail or Microsoft mailbox | Send from a sender on your domain |
| `sending_limit_reached` | The daily or monthly sending limit is reached | Retry after the limit resets, or move to a higher plan |
| `no_active_plan` | The account has no active plan | Choose a plan |
| `account_restricted`, `sending_paused` | Sending is paused on the account | Contact us |
| `account_deletion_scheduled` | The account is scheduled for deletion | Cancel the deletion in Settings > Security |
| `send_refused` | Any other reason; `error` explains it | Follow `error`, or contact us |

`404` codes: `template_not_found`, `sender_not_found`, `email_sender_not_found`, `email_type_not_found`. A `202` with `state: "held"` is not an error: the email is accepted and waits for a short review (`held_reason: "review"`), then goes out on its own and a `sent` event follows.

**Status webhook.** Every status change of a transactional email is POSTed as JSON to the account's status webhook (`set_status_webhook`). Text messages have a webhook of their own (`channel: "sms"`), so this one receives email events only. Events: `sent` (accepted by Mailsoftly's mail servers for delivery), `delivered` (the receiving mail server accepted it), `bounced` (`detail.bounce_type` is `hard` or `soft`), `complained` (marked as spam) and `failed` (refused by the sending service). Every body carries `channel` (`email` here; text messages carry `sms`, see send_transactional_sms), `test_mode` (true for an email sent in API test mode) and `message_type`. Example body:

```json
{
  "event_id": "evt_3f9a1c7e5b2d8a4f6c0e1b9d",
  "event": "bounced",
  "message_id": "msg_7k2m9q4x1c8v5b3n6z0a2s4d",
  "reference_id": "APP-2026-000123",
  "channel": "email",
  "email": "jane.doe@example.com",
  "status": "bounced",
  "occurred_at": "2026-10-07T18:42:11.204Z",
  "detail": {
    "bounce_type": "hard",
    "description": "The receiving server permanently rejected the address."
  },
  "test_mode": false,
  "message_type": "transactional"
}
```

### Verifying a signature

Every event is signed like every other Mailsoftly webhook: `X-Mailsoftly-Event` carries the event name, `X-Mailsoftly-Event-Id` the `event_id`, and `X-Mailsoftly-Signature` the signed timestamp (`t=<unix time>,v1=<hex>`). The headers, the verification steps, a Ruby and a JavaScript verifier and a test vector for this body shape are under **Webhook signatures** at the top of this documentation. Use `event_id` to ignore duplicates: a retried event keeps the same `event_id`.

### Your secret

The secret is shown once, when the webhook is created and when you rotate it. If you lose it, rotate it (`set_status_webhook` with `rotate_secret`). Rotation takes effect at once, with no overlap: requests are signed with the new secret from that moment, so give it to your server right away.

### Retries and acknowledgement

Answer with any 2xx within 10 seconds. Anything else is retried with growing waits, 10 attempts over about 4.5 hours, with the same `event_id`, so de-duplicate on it. Events can arrive out of order; `occurred_at` and `status` (the message's status after the event) settle it. After 100 events in a row that could not be delivered, the webhook is switched off; `set_status_webhook` with `enabled: true` switches it back on.

**Not every receiving server confirms acceptance.** A message can stay at `sent` with no `delivered` event. Treat `sent` with no later `bounced` or `failed` as accepted.

post.description:
Sends one text message (SMS) to one phone number and answers at once with a `message_id`. Use it for application messages: verification codes, reminders, delivery and appointment notices.

Text messaging is switched on per account by our team; until it is, the call is refused with `403 sms_not_enabled`. The account sends from its own registered number: `from_number` picks one of its numbers, otherwise the account's default number is used.

`to` is one phone number in international (E.164) format, for example `+14085551234`. `body` is plain text; merge tags render with the fields of the account's contact whose mobile phone is `to`. `first_name`, `last_name` and `fields` (values for custom fields that already exist, see `create_custom_field`) are written to that contact before the message renders. This operation never creates a contact: when no contact has this mobile phone, the merge tags render from the values passed with the call. Links are sent exactly as written: they are not shortened, rewritten or tracked.

**Opt-out line and length.** The first message a number sends to a phone, and every `marketing` message, ends with the line `Reply STOP to opt out.` The message can be at most 1,600 characters after merge tags and that line; longer is refused with `422 body_too_long`. The response's `segments` is the number of SMS parts the message is sent as, opt-out line included: up to 160 characters per part, or 70 when the text has characters outside the standard SMS alphabet (most emoji and accented letters), and fewer per part once a message needs several.

**Opt-outs.** A recipient who replies STOP (or STOPALL, UNSUBSCRIBE, CANCEL, END, QUIT, OPTOUT, REVOKE) to any of the account's numbers is opted out of the whole account, and further sends to that phone are refused with `422 recipient_opted_out`. Replying START opts back in. A STOP that arrives after a message was accepted still stops it: the message then gets a `failed` event with `detail.reason: "opted_out"`.

**Monthly limit.** Each account has a monthly limit counted in SMS parts, the way carriers bill: a message counts once for each part it is sent in (the response's `segments`). It is set from the volume declared when the account's number was registered (10,000 until then). Parts count from the first day of the calendar month (UTC); test messages and messages that failed before they left do not count. A message whose parts would take the account past the limit is refused with `422 sending_limit_reached`, until the next month or until our team raises the limit.

`202` with `state: "queued"` means the message is on its way; `state: "held"` means it waits for a short review and leaves once released. Pass `idempotency_key` to make retries safe: a second call with the same key returns the first message (`200`, `idempotent_replay: true`) instead of sending again. `reference_id` is echoed on every status event and accepted by `get_message_status`.

**Test mode.** While none of the account's numbers can send yet (no number, or its registration is not approved), text messages are test messages on their own, with nothing to switch on: they are accepted without a number but nothing leaves and no phone receives them. Each message gets a `sent` and a `delivered` event with `test_mode: true`, so you can build your status handling before your number is registered. Test messages share the account's allowance of 100 test messages a day with test emails (`422 test_mode_limit_reached`, with `resets_at`). As soon as one of the account's numbers can send, every text message sent through the API is real.

**Refusals.** When a message cannot go out, nothing is sent or stored. The answer is `422` (`403` for `sms_not_enabled`) with one of these codes and an `error` sentence that says what to fix.

| code | Meaning | Fix |
|------|---------|-----|
| `sms_not_enabled` (403) | Text messaging is not switched on for the account | Contact us |
| `invalid_to` | `to` is not one phone number in international format | Pass a number like `+14085551234` |
| `body_required` | `body` is missing or empty after merge tags | Pass `body` |
| `body_too_long` | Over 1,600 characters after merge tags and the opt-out line | Shorten `body` |
| `invalid_message_type` | `message_type` is not `transactional` or `marketing` | Use one of the two |
| `reference_id_too_long`, `idempotency_key_too_long` | Over 255 characters | Shorten it |
| `no_sms_number` | `from_number` is not one of the account's numbers | Pass one of the account's numbers, or leave `from_number` out |
| `sms_number_not_ready` | `from_number` names a number whose registration is not complete, while another number can send | Wait for the registration, or leave `from_number` out |
| `recipient_opted_out` | The phone replied STOP to the account | Do not send to it; the recipient can reply START |
| `sending_limit_reached` | The account's monthly limit is reached, or this message's parts would go over it | Shorten the message, wait for the next month, or contact us to raise it |
| `test_mode_limit_reached` | The account is in API test mode and today's 100 test messages are used | Wait for `resets_at` |
| `account_restricted`, `sending_paused` | Sending is paused on the account | Contact us |
| `send_refused` | The message cannot be sent | Contact us if it keeps happening |

**Status events.** Text message events go to the account's SMS status webhook (`set_status_webhook` with `channel: "sms"`, or the SMS Developers page in Mailsoftly), which has its own URL and signing secret and is signed and retried the same way as the email one. Email events never go there, and text message events never go to the email webhook. `get_message_status` answers for both. SMS payloads carry `channel: "sms"`, `from` (the account's number that sent the message) and `to` (the recipient) in place of `email`; `phone` repeats the recipient for integrations built before `from` and `to`. Events: `sent` (accepted by Mailsoftly's SMS service for delivery), `delivered` (the recipient's mobile carrier accepted it; `detail.confirmed_by` is `carrier`, or `handset` when the phone itself confirmed it. US carriers do not always confirm arrival on the phone, so `carrier` is the usual final answer) and `failed` (`detail.reason` says why, for example `invalid_number`, `blocked`, `unreachable`, `expired`, `opted_out` or `unknown`). Every message reaches `delivered` or `failed`.

**Replies.** When a recipient texts one of the account's numbers, a `replied` event goes to the SMS webhook with the reply in `detail.body`. `message_id` names the message being answered, or is `null` when the reply answers none of the account's messages (it is still sent). `from` is the number that replied and `to` is the account's number it reached; `phone` repeats the number that replied. `detail.keyword` is `stop`, `start` or `help` when the whole reply is one of the opt-out words, otherwise `null`: after `stop` the phone is opted out of the account's texts and further sends are refused with `recipient_opted_out`, after `start` it can be texted again, and `help` is answered automatically. A reply never changes the status of the message it answers; `status` in the body is that message's status (`null` without one). Each reply is its own event, so one message can have several, and `get_message_status` lists them in its event history. Example body:

```json
{
  "event_id": "evt_8c1d4e2f9a0b7c3d5e6f1a2b",
  "event": "replied",
  "message_id": "msg_7k2m9q4x1c8v5b3n6z0a2s4d",
  "reference_id": "APPT-2026-000456",
  "channel": "sms",
  "from": "+14085551234",
  "to": "+18885550100",
  "phone": "+14085551234",
  "status": "delivered",
  "occurred_at": "2026-10-07T18:44:02.518Z",
  "detail": {
    "body": "STOP",
    "keyword": "stop"
  },
  "test_mode": false,
  "message_type": "transactional"
}
```

Uses exactly the vocabulary of `POST /create_automation` (trigger table, step kinds, branching). `steps` replaces the whole step tree, so it carries the full list; get_automation returns the current tree in this same shape.

Its `steps` are refused (422): change one step with `POST /update_automation_step`, or deactivate the automation with `POST /update_automation_status` before replacing the tree. The rest of the automation is untouched, and the step keeps its id, so its results in get_automation_stats continue. Other step kinds change through `POST /update_automation`.

On an **active** automation this needs the `campaigns:send` scope (403 `insufficient_scope` otherwise), the same as switching it on, because it changes what contacts receive.

Contacts who enter after the edit get the new version. Contacts already in the automation keep the version they entered with, unless `apply_to_contacts_in_flow` is true: then those who have not reached this step yet get the new version too. Changes to the template's own content (`POST /update_email_template`) reach every contact who has not been sent it, either way, because the template is read when the email sends.

post.description:
Updates an existing contact's fields. Only the fields present in the request body are updated. All other fields remain unchanged.

`date_of_birth` takes `YYYY-MM-DD`, or `--MM-DD` for a birthday without its year. Other forms such as `05/12/1990` are read too; when nothing in the value says which part is the day, it is read month first for accounts in the United States and day first elsewhere. post.description: Edit an unsent draft in place: subject, body, name, reply_to, the audience, or restart it from a saved template. The audience takes the same fields as create_emails: `contact_list_id` for one list, or `contact_list_ids`, `segment_ids`, `exclude_contact_list_ids` and `exclude_segment_ids`. Passing any of those four replaces the whole audience (include and exclude), and the same refusals apply (`audience_conflict`, `audience_too_many`, `contact_list_not_found`, `segment_not_found`, `audience_not_enabled`). Body rules are the same as create_emails (body_format `content` or `html`). Sent campaigns cannot be edited. The from address is editable the same way create_emails sets it: exactly one of `sender_id` or `email_sender_id`, both taken from `GET /list_senders`. That is the way off a mailbox this credential cannot send from, and off a domain that has not finished DNS authentication.

contact_list_id.description: Make the draft a single-list campaign on this list (replaces any segment or multi-list audience). Not combinable with contact_list_ids.

contact_list_ids.description: Lists to send to, from list_contact_lists. Together with segment_ids this is the audience: everyone on any of them gets the campaign once, even when an address is on several (matched case-insensitively). One list here is the same as contact_list_id. Not combinable with contact_list_id or recipients. Include and exclude entries together are capped at 15.

email_sender_id.description: New from address as a connected mailbox or the shared address, from a kind 'gmail_mailbox', 'outlook_mailbox' or 'shared_fallback' entry of list_senders. Mutually exclusive with sender_id.

exclude_contact_list_ids.description: Lists whose members never get this campaign, even when they are also on an included list or segment.

exclude_segment_ids.description: Segments whose members never get this campaign, even when they are also on an included list or segment.

id.description: Draft id from create_emails or list_campaigns

segment_ids.description: Segments to send to, from list_segments. Members are worked out again at send time.

sender_id.description: New from address as a teammate on an authenticated sending domain, from a kind 'user' entry of list_senders. Mutually exclusive with email_sender_id.

template_id.description: Replace the body and design with a saved template
